prompt: A printer is on sale for much less than a rival model, but its replacement cartridges cost far more and last for fewer pages. Sam prints regularly for coursework. Which comparison helps Sam choose wisely?

options.text: Work out the total cost over the first year — printer plus the cartridges the expected printing will use — for both models, and compare those figures
Choose the cheaper shelf price, because running costs are too uncertain to think about
Choose the more expensive printer, because a higher price always means lower running costs
Ask which printer looks better on a desk, since the costs will even out anyway

explanation: The shelf price is only part of what a printer costs. For a regular printer user, adding the cartridges a year of printing will actually use can easily reverse which model is cheaper overall.
